final.investment_thesis:
The weighing verdict is Hold, and it is a verdict reached after testing both sides rather than a refuge from conflict.

Why the equity case cannot be zeroed. The bull never lost on business quality: nine-month revenue $364.4B, +16.15%, roughly triple AAPL's historical growth rate; Q3 gross margin 50.06% with cost of revenue +8.6% against revenue +16.4%, the cleanest signature of mix and pricing leverage; EPS +22.42% even after a ~219 bps tax step-up; free cash flow $110.2B, +52.5%, with OCF/NI at 1.15x so there is no accounting flattery; net cash up $28.5B in nine months to $62.2B with no long-term debt issued and D/E from 1.34x to 0.78x. The trend is intact: price is 10.67% above a 200-day at 281.30 that has risen 26 straight sessions, the 50-day sits above it, and the 15-session base has printed four higher lows while holding the 310.69 gap edge. That is why 0% is the wrong answer and why the bear's own concession matters: he does not call AAPL a structural short, and his preferred entry of 302-306 is only 2-3% below spot, so the dispute is about price, not about the asset.

Why the tape and the margin question block any add. The 10-Q was accepted 2026-07-31 at 10:01 ET; AAPL opened 304.81 and closed 308.91, -7.35% on 132.5M shares, the largest volume in the visible dataset, and it remains 6.6% below the pre-report close and 9.7% below the 344.57 high. That is the market's strongest single verdict on exactly the fundamentals being cited, and nothing in this evidence set reconciles it. The 08-20 session added an outside reversal: open 317.46, high 320.28 (a new base high), close 311.30, 0.65 points off the low, with the 20-day mean at 315.52 above price - two consecutive rejections in a two-point zone (319.28, then 320.28) beneath a 315.52-320.28 resistance stack. The arithmetic is unfavourable: from 311.30 the ratio to the 320.28 rejection is +2.89% against -3.63% to the 300.00 floor, about 0.80:1, and the bull's own breakout structure is only ~0.97:1 to its own first target. The bull himself designated margin as his thesis-breaker, and four headwinds converge on the 50.06% record gross margin simultaneously: the EU framework effective October 1 (IAP 30% to 26%, alt-payment 20%, link-out 15%, 5% CTC) hitting the highest-margin line; Samsung advanced foundry pricing reportedly up to 15%; raw materials up 260% with inventory days from ~9.4 to ~16.3, which converts into future COGS; and R&D +32.5%, now 9.34% of revenue. Rounding it out, 2.4 points of the 22.42% EPS growth is buyback, repurchases fell 12% ($70.6B to $62.1B), the effective tax rate climbs each quarter (15.39% to 17.58% to 17.86%), and at ~35x a ~$8.90 FY26 EPS estimate a de-rating to 28x is $249 on unchanged fundamentals.

Sizing: why 3.0% is the right total exposure, tested against 7% and 0%. This is a from-scratch reassessment, not a haircut applied to yesterday's holding. At 311.30 AAPL sits directly on the 310.69 gap edge, inside a ~3.5% box between a 315.52-320.28 ceiling that has rejected twice and a 300.00 floor that has held four times (07-31 low 300.00, 08-03 302.56, 08-12 300.57, 08-13 302.05), in a tape with a 2.51% daily ATR. 3.0% is the size that expresses 'real business, unresolved price'. The 7% alternative would require buying roughly $4,000 more (~12.8 shares, ~$4 in fees) under a rejection high into a sub-1:1 near-term ratio while the margin question is live - that is paying full price for an unresolved risk, and it only becomes justified on confirmation or in the 302-306 band where the risk/reward flips. The 0% alternative fails for a different reason: liquidation costs only ~$3 at 10 bps and cost is not the obstacle; the obstacle is that AAPL has printed two >6% single-day gaps in five weeks, so zeroing a coiled base means re-entry happens through a gap rather than at a price chosen in advance. The gap risk is symmetric - it cuts both ways - which is precisely why the answer is neither full exposure nor zero.

Practical purpose of the small position, not an observation stake. Observing evidence requires no shares. The 3.0% position is held because the fee-efficient way to own a confirmation-driven resolution with a defined invalidation is a small funded position plus dry powder, not a round trip in and out of a 3% box. Its contribution is explicit and bounded: +10% adds ~$300 (+0.30% of total equity), -10% costs ~$300 (-0.30%), and full downside to the 300.00 invalidation is ~-3.6% on the position (~-0.11% of total equity).

Cash opportunity cost, stated plainly. 97% of the account earns nothing because cash pays no interest. If AAPL fills the 310.69 to 329.59 gap (+5.9%) and runs to 333.43 (+7.1%), the 3.0% ticket captures only ~+0.18% to +0.21% of total equity while the other 97% earns zero - a real cost, and the reason I do not go below 3% and why the add conditions are explicit rather than vague. It does not override the downside case: the de-rating scenario (multiple normalization) is larger than the gap-fill scenario and would hit a 7% position roughly five times harder than a 3% one. Neither risk avoidance nor cash opportunity cost automatically wins here; they are close to offsetting, which is exactly what a Hold at 3.0% prices.

Resolving the one disagreement in the debate. The aggressive seat wanted a pre-positioned 302-306 accumulation and a scale to 5-6% on a 320.28 break; the conservative and neutral seats insisted on post-close confirmation only. The conservative/neutral construction wins: a pre-positioned add in a name that has gapped >6% twice in five weeks relies on a stop that can be skipped, and the 08-18/08-19 advance itself came on only 101% and 95% of average volume, so the 65M bar was weak. I adopt the stricter confirmation bar rather than the more permissive one. All three seats agreeing on 3.0% is convergence from three different mandates (alpha capture, asset protection, risk budgeting), not a manufactured compromise.

Rating: Hold, and it is a weighing verdict. The case against a zero is business quality plus an intact primary trend; the case against adding is the unreconciled 07-31 verdict, a double rejection at resistance, ~0.80:1 near-term ratio, and record-margin risk at ~35x. Both sides are live and offsetting at this price. That is Hold with keep_shares and target_weight_now null - preserving shares rather than rebalancing - not Underweight, because the bear's own entry band is only 2-3% lower and the primary trend is intact, and not Overweight, because nothing has confirmed.

What would change it (narrative conditions only, not implemented orders, separate from today's keep_shares). Add trigger: a daily close above 320.28 on >=90M shares - the stricter bar adopted over 65M, since 65M was only ~125% of a depressed 20-day average (~53M) - on which scale toward 5-6% in one step. Value zone: 302-306, above the 300.00 base floor, with hard stop below 299.00 (1.5 ATR from spot is 299.59, which confluences with the base floor); both sides endorse this band as the place where risk/reward genuinely improves. Hard invalidation: a decisive close below 300.00 on expanding volume breaks the 15-session base and confirms the bounce as a failed retest - cut toward 0% and do not average down. Sizing note: because AAPL has gapped >6% twice in five weeks, any add should be sized at roughly half the ATR-implied amount, since stops can gap through entirely.

Missing evidence flagged rather than assumed away: no guidance detail or color from the 2026-07-31 print, so the -7.35% reaction is unexplained by anything in the dataset; the news sample is 20 of 118 records with nothing for Aug 13-17; insider activity is unavailable; and the +91% net intangibles build against +$13.5B other noncurrent liabilities with no acquisition cash-out line is genuinely unresolved - the bull's 'investment in the moat' reading is a plausible assumption, not evidence, and the bear is right to refuse to underwrite it at 35x. Any of these, once supplied, could move this to Overweight or Underweight quickly.
final.time_horizon: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print
